str` to enums in `crates/cachet-core/src/stats.rs`:

- `StatKind`: `Narinfo, Nar, Part, Begin, Complete, Abort, Probe, Lease, Sweep,
  Unknown`.
- `StatOutcome`: `EdgeHit, BucketHit, Miss, Stored, Answered, Status(u16)`,
  where `Status` renders as three digits and parses only three digits.

That refactor pays a second debt. Today nothing mechanically ties
`StatPoint::blobs()`'s column order to `QueryDimension::column()`'s mapping,
and `crates/cachet-core/src/stats.rs:253` names the risk in a comment. With
both sides speaking enums, one test can assert the round trip instead of two
tests asserting halves.

`repository`, `reference`, and `project` stay unfilterable. Their values are
open strings, and admitting one would put caller text into a statement that
runs with the deployment's Cloudflare token. ADR 0015 records the choice so a
later reader knows it was a decision.

### 1c. `by=project` stops being a question with no answer

`StatPoint::for_project` (`crates/cachet-core/src/stats.rs:194`) has no call
site outside its own unit test, so `blob6` is always the empty string and
`by=project` can only ever return one empty row. The lease name is the
repository with a hyphen, which `blob4` already carries, so the dimension is
redundant rather than unimplemented. Remove `Project` from `QueryDimension`
and remove `for_project`, leaving `blob6` reserved and empty with a `// why:`
comment, because renumbering the columns would misread every point already
written.

### 1d. Writes count their bytes

`count_write` gains a byte count read from the request's `content-length` at
the router, where `write_kind` already reads the branch. The definition is
bytes that crossed the wire on this request: the compressed NAR on a whole
PUT, the part on a part PUT, and zero for begin, complete, and abort. That is
what the bucket gained, and it is the number Overview's "17.8 GB" means. The
`double2` row in DEPLOY.md's column table says so.

### 1e. The deployment binds what the counter route reads

The route reads three configuration values and the deployment supplies two.
`infra/alchemy.run.ts:56` sets `CACHET_STATS_DATASET` and, when configured,
`CACHET_STATS_TOKEN`, and never sets `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, which
`crates/cachet-worker/src/api.rs:142` reads on every request. Bind it beside
the other two.

The account id is an identifier rather than a credential, and it keeps its
unprefixed name for the reason DEPLOY.md already gives: it is the variable
every Cloudflare tool in the shell reads. `infra/src/config.ts` learns it from
`process.env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, the same variable the deploy already
requires for alchemy's own authentication.

A stats token with no account id is a deployment that counts and silently
cannot report, so `loadStageConfig` refuses that pair by name. That file's
stated law is that a deploy which cannot configure itself fails before
touching the account, and this is exactly such a case.

### 1f. The lane binds the dataset and finally sees a 200

`workerd/wrangler.toml` gains an `[[analytics_engine_datasets]]` block for
`CACHET_EVENTS`, which alone moves `stats::emit` from an early return to its
real path in every scenario: the builder construction and the blob and double
marshalling start running under test. Confirm miniflare accepts the binding
type when wiring it; if it refuses, the writer's coverage stays in the unit
lane and the doc says so rather than implying a coverage the lane does not
have.

The read side needs one more seam. `run_stats_sql` hardcodes
`https://api.cloudflare.com/...`, so no test can reach its success path. Give
the base URL a variable, `CACHET_STATS_API_URL`, exactly as `CACHET_JWKS_URL`
and `CACHET_GITHUB_API_URL` already work, and point it at the workerd driver's
stub server alongside the lane's `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`,
`CACHET_STATS_DATASET`, and a `CACHET_STATS_TOKEN` entering through
`.dev.vars` the way the signing secret already does.

The stub earns more than one assertion. It receives the composed SQL as a
plain text body, so it can assert the statement byte-for-byte before answering
canned rows, which turns the query builder into a wire-level contract in place
of the four substring assertions it has today. With that in place the lane
covers, for the first time: the 200 path, `SqlRow` deserialization, the
response shaping, the zero fill, the emitted SQL for each subject, dimension,
window, and filter combination, and the refusal of an inadmissible
`(bucket, window)` pair. The existing 503 rows stay, moved to a scenario that
deliberately unsets the token, so "counts but cannot report" remains a tested
answer rather than becoming an accident.

### 1g. `GET /api/whoami`

The console needs to know who it is before it renders anything. The route sits
outside `/api/self/` because it must answer for an org member who is not an
admin, and `/api/self/*` is admin-gated by documented contract.

```json
{ "login": "shivansh", "admin": true, "credential": "browser",
  "expiresAtMs": 1789000000000 }
```

`credential` comes from the `ReadIdentity` variant (`browser`, `laptop`, or
`ci`), and `expiresAtMs` is present only for a session. An unauthenticated
request answers 401, which the console reads as "show the sign-in screen"
rather than as an error.

### 1h. A browser session stops being a cache-read credential

A session cookie reads cache contents today. `read_routes`
(`crates/cachet-worker/src/lib.rs:343`) authorizes narinfo and NAR reads
through `verdict::authorize_read`, which accepts the cookie and answers
`ReadIdentity::Session` with no scope attached, and nothing downstream
distinguishes that identity from a laptop's. Meanwhile `resolve_session`
(`crates/cachet-worker/src/verdict.rs:400`) checks only that the record is
younger than its 14-day TTL, so it never re-checks org membership. The two
facts together mean a copy of an ex-member's cookie substitutes from the cache
for a fortnight after they leave the org.

Give the session identity a scope: it authenticates the console's own surface
(`/api/self/*`, `/api/whoami`, `/api/probe` for the search field, and
`/roots`) and is refused on the object paths that serve cache bytes. Nix never
sends a cookie, so nothing legitimate loses a credential, and the browser
becomes see-only in fact rather than by assumption. The refusal is
`ClientError::Unauthorized`, the same answer an anonymous read gets, and the
workerd lane asserts it on both a narinfo and a NAR.

The statistics window then stands as an accepted trade: a session outlives org
removal by up to 14 days for counters and GC reports, and
`docs/security/threat-model.md:64` gets corrected to say that rather than
claiming a 600s verdict re-check the code never performs.

Closing the statistics window too would mean storing the GitHub token on the
session record and re-checking membership the way ADR 0002 already does for
laptops. That is a second GitHub credential at rest in KV for a window you
have judged acceptable, so this plan does not take it. ADR 0016 records both
the scope and the trade, so the choice is legible later.

### 1i. The two verbatim bodies get schemas

`GET /api/self/gc-runs/{runId}` and `GET /roots/{project}` stream stored JSON

mirror schemas in `cachet-api` with a unit test asserting each mirror

### Files phase 1 touches

`crates/cachet-core/src/auth.rs` (the session record),
`crates/cachet-worker/src/api.rs`, `crates/cachet-worker/src/lib.rs`,
`crates/cachet-worker/src/verdict.rs`, `crates/cachet-worker/src/oauth.rs`,
`crates/cachet-api/src/routes.rs`, `crates/cachet-api/src/lib.rs`,
`infra/alchemy.run.ts`, `infra/src/config.ts`, `workerd/check.mjs`,
`workerd/wrangler.toml`, `docs/openapi.yaml` (generated), `docs/DEPLOY.md`,
`docs/security/threat-model.md`.

### Gates phase 1 pays

`just unit`, `just property`, `just golden`, `just openapi` then
`just openapi-check`, `just wasm`, `just workerd`, `just clippy`,
`just clippy-wasm`.

---

## Phase 2: the deployment serves the console

### 2a. The asset binding

`infra/alchemy.run.ts` gains one property on the existing `Cloudflare.Worker`

`assets` and `runWorkerFirst`, and confirm the exact `AssetsProps` field names
there rather than from the website docs.

```ts
assets: {
  directory: "../web/dist",
  // why: the Rust router is the only authority over paths. An asset rule
  // that answered a /{hash}.narinfo miss with index.html would serve every
  // nix substituter 200 text/html where it expects a 404.
  runWorkerFirst: true,
},
```

`bundle: false` and `main: ../crates/cachet-worker/build/index.js` stay as they
are. Assets upload beside the wasm bundle; rolldown never sees either.

### 2b. The Rust side

A new `crates/cachet-worker/src/console.rs` owns two functions and the router
gains one branch ahead of the protocol paths:

- `owns(path)` answers true for `/console` and anything under `/console/`.
- `serve(env, req, path)` fetches from `env.assets("ASSETS")` (workers-rs
  0.8.5 has `Env::assets`), and rewrites a path with no file extension to
  `/console/index.html` so a deep link into the router serves the shell.
- `GET /` answers 302 to `/console`.

A deployment whose worker predates the binding must degrade rather than fail:
a missing `ASSETS` binding answers 404 for `/console`, exactly as today. That
mirrors the stats binding's existing contract, where a worker older than the
dataset counts nothing and serves exactly as well.

### 2c. The lane proves the law

`workerd/wrangler.toml` gains an `[assets]` block pointing at a small
committed fixture directory, `workerd/fixtures/assets/`, holding an
`index.html` and one hashed file. The fixture keeps `just workerd` free of a
Vite build, and the real bundle's serving is proven live by the integration
lane instead.

The new scenario asserts, in one boot: `/` redirects to `/console`; `/console`
serves the shell; `/console/traffic` serves the shell; `/console/assets/x.js`
serves the file with its own content type; `/nix-cache-info` is unchanged; and
**a `/{hash}.narinfo` read for an absent path still answers 404 problem+json
with assets bound**. That last row is the one that matters, and it is the
reason the routing decision lives in Rust.

### 2d. The callback stops needing configuration

`CACHET_UI_ORIGIN` is today the verbatim `Location` of the post-login 302, and
a deployment that leaves it unset answers 204 instead
(`crates/cachet-core/src/oauth.rs:131`). With the console at the deployment's
own host, the default becomes `https://{CACHET_HOST}/console`, so the browser
flow works with no operator configuration at all. Keep the variable as an
override for anyone hosting a UI elsewhere, and update the DEPLOY.md row and
`scripts/bootstrap.sh`'s generated env file to say what it now means.

### Files phase 2 touches

`infra/alchemy.run.ts`, `crates/cachet-worker/src/console.rs` (new),
`crates/cachet-worker/src/lib.rs`, `crates/cachet-core/src/oauth.rs`,
`workerd/wrangler.toml`, `workerd/fixtures/assets/` (new),
`workerd/check.mjs`, `scripts/bootstrap.sh`, `docs/DEPLOY.md`.

---

## Phase 3: the console

### 3a. The workspace

A `web/` directory at the repository root, built by bun and Vite, both already
in the devshell (`nix/devshell.nix` carries `pkgs.bun` and `pkgs.nodejs_22`).
`bun.lock` commits, and the build runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` the way

Runtime dependencies, each with the `// why:` comment §6 requires, in the
`package.json`:

| Package | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `react`, `react-dom` | The view layer. |
| `@tanstack/react-router` | Typed routes and typed search parameters, so a filtered Traffic view is a link someone can send. SPA mode; no TanStack Start, because the worker serves static assets and an SSR entry would collide with `main: build/index.js`. |
| `@tanstack/react-query` | Polling, caching, and refetch on focus for a dashboard that reads six routes. |
| `@stylexjs/stylex`, `@stylexjs/unplugin` | Atomic styles compiled at build time, with the design tokens as the only source of scale values. |
| `@base-ui/react` | Headless primitives for the segmented controls, menus, and tooltips the screens use. |
| `motion` | The counter and chart transitions that make the console feel alive rather than repainted. |
| `effect` | `Schema` decodes API responses and URL search parameters through the same closed vocabulary the Rust enums define. Pinned to the exact version `infra/` already pins. |
| `@fontsource-variable/geist`, `-geist-mono` | The shipped faces, both OFL. |

Vite builds with `base: "/console/"` to `web/dist`.

### 3b. Tokens and fonts

`web/src/styles/tokens.stylex.ts` carries the Paper file's token values
verbatim: the `--color-*` set, the `--text-*` scale, `--font-weight-*`,

the licensed face first and the shipped one behind it:

```
--font-mono:    "Berkeley Mono", "Geist Mono", ui-monospace, monospace
--font-display: "Neue Haas Grotesk Display Pro", "Geist", system-ui, sans-serif
```

The flag is one optional stylesheet. `/api/public/config` gains a nullable

single `<link rel="stylesheet">` when it is present. With the flag off, which
is the default, the licensed families resolve to nothing and Geist Mono
renders. With it on, the CDN's `@font-face` rules make them resolve. Nothing
about the bundle changes between the two, so deployment identity stays
configuration (ADR 0010) and no licensed byte enters the repository.

trust surface, so `docs/security/threat-model.md` gains a sentence naming it
and the default-off posture.

The shell is shared by all five and matches the Paper structure: a `hud-strip`
across the top, a 64px `rail` of navigation icons, a `header` carrying the
breadcrumb and the search field, the `content` region, and a `status-bar`

Each screen's data sources, all of which exist after phase 1:

| Screen | Reads |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | `/api/self/stats`, `/api/self/gc-runs` for the 30-run line, `/api/self/events?subject=reads&window=week`, `?subject=writes&by=repository&window=week` |

Six states need design before they need code, and each one is reachable today:

- **Signed out.** `/api/whoami` answers 401. The console shows a sign-in

- **Org member who is not an admin.** `admin: false`. Access renders; the

- **Loading.** Skeletons rather than spinners, gated so a fast answer never

- **Fresh deployment.** `/api/self/stats` answers 404 by design when no

1. `docs/testing/console.md`
2. `[lane.console]` with a summary in `docs/testing/lanes.toml`

### Files phase 3 touches

`web/` (new: `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`,

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/testing/lanes.toml`,

## Approved Plan:
# The cachet console

## Context

The Paper file `Nox / Cachet · Console` holds five finished 1440x900 screens:
Overview, Garbage collection, Access, Traffic, and Laptops. Nothing in the
repository serves them. There is no `.tsx`, no `.css`, no `.html`, and no
bundler config anywhere, the only `package.json` outside the generated worker
build directory is `infra/`, and the worker answers `GET /` with an RFC 9457
`not_found`.

Most of the plumbing is already in place. `require_admin`
(`crates/cachet-worker/src/verdict.rs:501`) accepts `ReadIdentity::Session`,
so a browser that finished the OAuth flow can already call all four
`/api/self/*` routes; the session cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax on
`Path=/`, which works when the console is served from the worker's own origin
and fails anywhere else. CLAUDE.md §1 and `crates/cachet-worker/src/api.rs:2`
both call the console "the future SPA". This is that work.

Four gaps sit between the screens and the data. Two are in the counter route:
`/api/self/events` groups by `kind|outcome|actor|repository|reference|project`
with no time bucket, so the per-day lines on Traffic and Laptops have no query
behind them, and it takes no filter, so "laptop reads by outcome", which is
the whole Laptops screen, cannot be asked. The third is in the writer:
Overview's "Pushed this week, 1,904 paths, 17.8 GB" wants bytes per write, and
`count_write` (`crates/cachet-worker/src/lib.rs:286`) never calls
`.measuring(...)`, so every write point carries `double2 = 0`. The fourth is
identity: no route tells a browser who it is, so a console can only learn
whether it is an admin by receiving a 403.

Underneath all four sits a binding bug that makes the counter route
unanswerable. `crates/cachet-worker/src/api.rs:142` reads
`env.var("CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID")` on every request, and `infra/alchemy.run.ts`
never binds it: a grep for `ACCOUNT_ID` across `infra/` returns nothing. So
`GET /api/self/events` answers 503 `storage_unavailable` on every deployment,
including one that sets `CACHET_DEPLOY_STATS_TOKEN`, and has done since the
route shipped in #24. The counting works, because `CACHET_EVENTS` is bound;
the reporting has never once run.

The reason nobody noticed is the second half of the same gap. The successful
path of that route has no test coverage of any kind. `workerd/wrangler.toml`
binds no Analytics Engine dataset and sets none of `CACHET_STATS_TOKEN`,
`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, or `CACHET_STATS_DATASET`, so all six lane rows
(`workerd/check.mjs:1868`) are refused at the config check before any query
runs, and `stats::emit` returns early at `crates/cachet-worker/src/stats.rs:22`
in every scenario. `run_stats_sql`, the `SqlRow` deserialization, the response
shaping, and the whole writer path are untested, and every chart in the
console would ride all of them.

## Decisions taken

The console is served by the deployment itself, from the worker's own origin,
with the Rust router as the only authority over paths. `GET /` redirects to
`/console`, and the console lives under that prefix.

The stack is chosen for craft rather than for a small dependency count: React
19, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, StyleX, Base UI, and motion, matching the
lynk dashboard's caliber so the two consoles read as related work. Effect's
`Schema` decodes both the wire and the URL search parameters, because the
console's vocabulary and the worker's closed enums should be the same
vocabulary.

Licensed faces load from your own CDN behind a flag that defaults to off. The
repository ships Geist Mono and Geist, and a deployment that sets the flag
gets Berkeley Mono and Neue Haas Grotesk Display Pro instead.

The browser session becomes see-only. It authenticates the console's surface
and is refused on the paths that serve cache bytes, which it can reach today.

---

## Phase 1: the counter route answers time and filtered questions

Everything here lands before the console starts, so the console builds against
a route that works and is tested.

### 1a. Time buckets

`crates/cachet-core/src/stats_query.rs` gains two variants on the existing
`QueryDimension` enum, `Hour` and `Day`, so `by=day` reads the way you
described it. A time variant differs from a blob variant in three ways, and
all three live in the same file:

- `column()` returns a time projection (`toStartOfHour(timestamp)` or
  `toStartOfDay(timestamp)`) rather than a blob name. Confirm the exact
  function against Cloudflare's Analytics Engine SQL reference during
  implementation; `intDiv(toUInt32(timestamp), 3600) * 3600` is the fallback
  that is certain to parse.
- The ordering becomes `ORDER BY dimension ASC`, because a chart reads left to
  right, where a dimension list reads largest first.
- The `LIMIT` becomes the bucket count the window implies rather than
  `STATS_ROWS_MAX`, and it stays an integer literal from an enum.

The pair `(bucket, window)` is itself validated: `hour` is admissible only
with `window=day` (24 buckets), and `day` with `week` (7) or `month` (30).
`by=hour&window=month` would ask for 720 rows against a cap of 100, so it
answers 400 `malformed_query` rather than silently truncating a series.

Analytics Engine returns no row for a bucket with no events, and a line chart
with a missing day is a lie, so the worker fills the gaps. Filling is pure
logic over `now` and the window, so it belongs in `cachet-core` beside the
query builder, and it gives the property lane a law: a bucketed answer always
carries exactly the expected number of rows, ascending, with no gaps and no
duplicates.

One constraint worth writing down where the code can see it. The platform
stamps the `timestamp` column at ingest, and the worker cannot set it:
`worker-sys-0.8.5`'s `writeDataPoint` takes indexes, doubles, and blobs and
nothing else. So `UnixMillis now` is not the `timestamp` column, points cannot
be replayed at chosen times, and the fill must align `now` down to a bucket
boundary rather than assume the two clocks agree.

### 1b. Filters drawn from the same closed enums

Three optional query parameters join the route: `actor=`, `kind=`, and
`outcome=`. Each parses into a closed enum or refuses, and each becomes one
`AND blob{n} = '{literal}'` clause, so the threat model's claim that no caller
text reaches SQL stays literally true.

Supporting that means promoting two writer-side vocabularies from `&'static
str` to enums in `crates/cachet-core/src/stats.rs`:

- `StatKind`: `Narinfo, Nar, Part, Begin, Complete, Abort, Probe, Lease, Sweep,
  Unknown`.
- `StatOutcome`: `EdgeHit, BucketHit, Miss, Stored, Answered, Status(u16)`,
  where `Status` renders as three digits and parses only three digits.

That refactor pays a second debt. Today nothing mechanically ties
`StatPoint::blobs()`'s column order to `QueryDimension::column()`'s mapping,
and `crates/cachet-core/src/stats.rs:253` names the risk in a comment. With
both sides speaking enums, one test can assert the round trip instead of two
tests asserting halves.

`repository`, `reference`, and `project` stay unfilterable. Their values are
open strings, and admitting one would put caller text into a statement that
runs with the deployment's Cloudflare token. ADR 0015 records the choice so a
later reader knows it was a decision.

### 1c. `by=project` stops being a question with no answer

`StatPoint::for_project` (`crates/cachet-core/src/stats.rs:194`) has no call
site outside its own unit test, so `blob6` is always the empty string and
`by=project` can only ever return one empty row. The lease name is the
repository with a hyphen, which `blob4` already carries, so the dimension is
redundant rather than unimplemented. Remove `Project` from `QueryDimension`
and remove `for_project`, leaving `blob6` reserved and empty with a `// why:`
comment, because renumbering the columns would misread every point already
written.

### 1d. Writes count their bytes

`count_write` gains a byte count read from the request's `content-length` at
the router, where `write_kind` already reads the branch. The definition is
bytes that crossed the wire on this request: the compressed NAR on a whole
PUT, the part on a part PUT, and zero for begin, complete, and abort. That is
what the bucket gained, and it is the number Overview's "17.8 GB" means. The
`double2` row in DEPLOY.md's column table says so.

### 1e. The deployment binds what the counter route reads

The route reads three configuration values and the deployment supplies two.
`infra/alchemy.run.ts:56` sets `CACHET_STATS_DATASET` and, when configured,
`CACHET_STATS_TOKEN`, and never sets `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, which
`crates/cachet-worker/src/api.rs:142` reads on every request. Bind it beside
the other two.

The account id is an identifier rather than a credential, and it keeps its
unprefixed name for the reason DEPLOY.md already gives: it is the variable
every Cloudflare tool in the shell reads. `infra/src/config.ts` learns it from
`process.env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, the same variable the deploy already
requires for alchemy's own authentication.

A stats token with no account id is a deployment that counts and silently
cannot report, so `loadStageConfig` refuses that pair by name. That file's
stated law is that a deploy which cannot configure itself fails before
touching the account, and this is exactly such a case.

### 1f. The lane binds the dataset and finally sees a 200

`workerd/wrangler.toml` gains an `[[analytics_engine_datasets]]` block for
`CACHET_EVENTS`, which alone moves `stats::emit` from an early return to its
real path in every scenario: the builder construction and the blob and double
marshalling start running under test. Confirm miniflare accepts the binding
type when wiring it; if it refuses, the writer's coverage stays in the unit
lane and the doc says so rather than implying a coverage the lane does not
have.

The read side needs one more seam. `run_stats_sql` hardcodes
`https://api.cloudflare.com/...`, so no test can reach its success path. Give
the base URL a variable, `CACHET_STATS_API_URL`, exactly as `CACHET_JWKS_URL`
and `CACHET_GITHUB_API_URL` already work, and point it at the workerd driver's
stub server alongside the lane's `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`,
`CACHET_STATS_DATASET`, and a `CACHET_STATS_TOKEN` entering through
`.dev.vars` the way the signing secret already does.

The stub earns more than one assertion. It receives the composed SQL as a
plain text body, so it can assert the statement byte-for-byte before answering
canned rows, which turns the query builder into a wire-level contract in place
of the four substring assertions it has today. With that in place the lane
covers, for the first time: the 200 path, `SqlRow` deserialization, the
response shaping, the zero fill, the emitted SQL for each subject, dimension,
window, and filter combination, and the refusal of an inadmissible
`(bucket, window)` pair. The existing 503 rows stay, moved to a scenario that
deliberately unsets the token, so "counts but cannot report" remains a tested
answer rather than becoming an accident.

### 1g. `GET /api/whoami`

The console needs to know who it is before it renders anything. The route sits
outside `/api/self/` because it must answer for an org member who is not an
admin, and `/api/self/*` is admin-gated by documented contract.

```json
{ "login": "shivansh", "admin": true, "credential": "browser",
  "expiresAtMs": 1789000000000 }
```

`credential` comes from the `ReadIdentity` variant (`browser`, `laptop`, or
`ci`), and `expiresAtMs` is present only for a session. An unauthenticated
request answers 401, which the console reads as "show the sign-in screen"
rather than as an error.

### 1h. A browser session stops being a cache-read credential

A session cookie reads cache contents today. `read_routes`
(`crates/cachet-worker/src/lib.rs:343`) authorizes narinfo and NAR reads
through `verdict::authorize_read`, which accepts the cookie and answers
`ReadIdentity::Session` with no scope attached, and nothing downstream
distinguishes that identity from a laptop's. Meanwhile `resolve_session`
(`crates/cachet-worker/src/verdict.rs:400`) checks only that the record is
younger than its 14-day TTL, so it never re-checks org membership. The two
facts together mean a copy of an ex-member's cookie substitutes from the cache
for a fortnight after they leave the org.

Give the session identity a scope: it authenticates the console's own surface
(`/api/self/*`, `/api/whoami`, `/api/probe` for the search field, and
`/roots`) and is refused on the object paths that serve cache bytes. Nix never
sends a cookie, so nothing legitimate loses a credential, and the browser
becomes see-only in fact rather than by assumption. The refusal is
`ClientError::Unauthorized`, the same answer an anonymous read gets, and the
workerd lane asserts it on both a narinfo and a NAR.

The statistics window then stands as an accepted trade: a session outlives org
removal by up to 14 days for counters and GC reports, and
`docs/security/threat-model.md:64` gets corrected to say that rather than
claiming a 600s verdict re-check the code never performs.

Closing the statistics window too would mean storing the GitHub token on the
session record and re-checking membership the way ADR 0002 already does for
laptops. That is a second GitHub credential at rest in KV for a window you
have judged acceptable, so this plan does not take it. ADR 0016 records both
the scope and the trade, so the choice is legible later.

### 1i. The two verbatim bodies get schemas

`GET /api/self/gc-runs/{runId}` and `GET /roots/{project}` stream stored JSON
verbatim, so `crates/cachet-api/src/routes.rs:435` declares them as untyped
`application/json` and the OpenAPI document describes their bodies not at all.
A typed console client wants both. Declare `GcReport` and `LeaseDocument` as
mirror schemas in `cachet-api` with a unit test asserting each mirror
round-trips the core type's JSON, because deriving `utoipa::ToSchema` on
`cachet-core` would put a derive macro dependency inside the pure crate and
cross §4's boundary.

### Files phase 1 touches

`crates/cachet-core/src/stats_query.rs`, `crates/cachet-core/src/stats.rs`,
`crates/cachet-core/src/auth.rs` (the session record),
`crates/cachet-worker/src/api.rs`, `crates/cachet-worker/src/lib.rs`,
`crates/cachet-worker/src/verdict.rs`, `crates/cachet-worker/src/oauth.rs`,

`workerd/wrangler.toml`, `docs/openapi.yaml` (generated), `docs/DEPLOY.md`,
`docs/security/threat-model.md`.

### Gates phase 1 pays

`just unit`, `just property`, `just golden`, `just openapi` then
`just openapi-check`, `just wasm`, `just workerd`, `just clippy`,

## Phase 2: the deployment serves the console

### 2a. The asset binding

`infra/alchemy.run.ts` gains one property on the existing `Cloudflare.Worker`

```ts

  directory: "../web/dist",
  // why: the Rust router is the only authority over paths. An asset rule
  // that answered a /{hash}.narinfo miss with index.html would serve every
  // nix substituter 200 text/html where it expects a 404.
  runWorkerFirst: true,

```

`bundle: false` and `main: ../crates/cachet-worker/build/index.js` stay as they

### 2b. The Rust side

A new `crates/cachet-worker/src/console.rs` owns two functions and the router

- `owns(path)` answers true for `/console` and anything under `/console/`.
- `serve(env, req, path)` fetches from `env.assets("ASSETS")` (workers-rs

### 2c. The lane proves the law

The new scenario asserts, in one boot: `/` redirects to `/console`; `/console`
serves the shell; `/console/traffic` serves the shell; `/console/assets/x.js`
serves the file with its own content type; `/nix-cache-info` is unchanged; and
**a `/{hash}.narinfo` read for an absent path still answers 404 problem+json

reason the routing decision lives in Rust.

`CACHET_UI_ORIGIN` is today the verbatim `Location` of the post-login 302, and
a deployment that leaves it unset answers 204 instead

own host, the default becomes `https://{CACHET_HOST}/console`, so the browser

`infra/alchemy.run.ts`, `crates/cachet-worker/src/console.rs` (new),
`crates/cachet-worker/src/lib.rs`, `crates/cachet-core/src/oauth.rs`,
`workerd/wrangler.toml`, `workerd/fixtures/assets/` (new),

## Phase 3: the console

### 3a. The workspace

A `web/` directory at the repository root, built by bun and Vite, both already

`bun.lock` commits, and the build runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` the way
`just deploy` already does for `infra/`.

Runtime dependencies, each with the `// why:` comment §6 requires, in the
`package.json`:

| Package | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `react`, `react-dom` | The view layer. |
| `@tanstack/react-router` | Typed routes and typed search parameters, so a filtered Traffic view is a link someone can send. SPA mode; no TanStack Start, because the worker serves static assets and an SSR entry would collide with `main: build/index.js`. |
| `@tanstack/react-query` | Polling, caching, and refetch on focus for a dashboard that reads six routes. |
| `@stylexjs/stylex`, `@stylexjs/unplugin` | Atomic styles compiled at build time, with the design tokens as the only source of scale values. |
| `@base-ui/react` | Headless primitives for the segmented controls, menus, and tooltips the screens use. |
| `motion` | The counter and chart transitions that make the console feel alive rather than repainted. |
| `effect` | `Schema` decodes API responses and URL search parameters through the same closed vocabulary the Rust enums define. Pinned to the exact version `infra/` already pins. |
| `@fontsource-variable/geist`, `-geist-mono` | The shipped faces, both OFL. |

Vite builds with `base: "/console/"` to `web/dist`.

### 3b. Tokens and fonts

`web/src/styles/tokens.stylex.ts` carries the Paper file's token values
verbatim: the `--color-*` set, the `--text-*` scale, `--font-weight-*`,
`--tracking-*`, `--leading-*`, and the spacing scale. Each font stack names
the licensed face first and the shipped one behind it:

```
--font-mono:    "Berkeley Mono", "Geist Mono", ui-monospace, monospace
--font-display: "Neue Haas Grotesk Display Pro", "Geist", system-ui, sans-serif
```

The flag is one optional stylesheet. `/api/public/config` gains a nullable
`fontCss` field sourced from a new `CACHET_FONT_CSS` variable
(`CACHET_DEPLOY_FONT_CSS` in the deploy contract), and the console appends a
single `<link rel="stylesheet">` when it is present. With the flag off, which
is the default, the licensed families resolve to nothing and Geist Mono
renders. With it on, the CDN's `@font-face` rules make them resolve. Nothing
about the bundle changes between the two, so deployment identity stays
configuration (ADR 0010) and no licensed byte enters the repository.

The console asking a third-party origin for fonts is a new fact about its
trust surface, so `docs/security/threat-model.md` gains a sentence naming it
and the default-off posture.

### 3c. The screens

The shell is shared by all five and matches the Paper structure: a `hud-strip`
across the top, a 64px `rail` of navigation icons, a `header` carrying the
breadcrumb and the search field, the `content` region, and a `status-bar`
naming the signed-in login and the host.

Each screen's data sources, all of which exist after phase 1:

| Screen | Reads |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | `/api/self/stats`, `/api/self/gc-runs` for the 30-run line, `/api/self/events?subject=reads&window=week`, `?subject=writes&by=repository&window=week` |
| Garbage collection | `/api/self/gc-runs`, `/api/self/gc-runs/{runId}` |
| Access | `/api/public/config`, `/api/whoami`, `POST /logout` |
| Traffic | `/api/self/events` with `subject` from the Reads/Writes/Probes control, `window` from Day/Week/Month, `by=hour|day` for the line and `by=outcome` for the table |
| Laptops | `/api/self/events?subject=reads&actor=laptop` grouped by `day` and by `outcome`, plus the unfiltered read total for the share |

Charts are hand-rolled SVG. The Paper file's chart is one area path, one line
path, one gridline, and an endpoint circle
(`panel-chart` under the Traffic artboard), so a charting library would carry
weight nothing here needs. The scales are pure functions in
`web/src/lib/`, which is where the console lane tests them.

Follow the repository's own convention for structure: route files do the
wiring, presentational components take props and no queries, and derivations
live in pure modules. That split is what makes the lane's component tests
possible without a mock framework.

### 3d. States the mockups do not cover

Six states need design before they need code, and each one is reachable today:

- **Signed out.** `/api/whoami` answers 401. The console shows a sign-in
  screen pointing at `/_auth/login`.
- **Org member who is not an admin.** `admin: false`. Access renders; the
  other four screens are hidden with a line naming `CACHET_ADMINS` as the
  reason.
- **Loading.** Skeletons rather than spinners, gated so a fast answer never
  flashes one.
- **Fresh deployment.** `/api/self/stats` answers 404 by design when no
  collection has finished (`crates/cachet-worker/src/api.rs:345`). Overview
  and Garbage collection must read that as "no run yet", never as an error.
- **Counting without reporting.** A deployment with no `CACHET_STATS_TOKEN`
  answers 503 `storage_unavailable` on `/api/self/events`. Traffic and Laptops
  must say that the deployment counts but cannot report, and point at the
  DEPLOY.md row.
- **A tripped GC gate.** `gate` is non-null on the run, which the Garbage
  collection screen already shows in red for one row; the same treatment
  belongs on Overview when the latest run tripped.

### 3e. The console lane

Per §9 every test belongs to exactly one lane, and a lane's id is its just
verb, its CI job, and its doc basename. The new lane is `console`:

1. `docs/testing/console.md`
2. `[lane.console]` with a summary in `docs/testing/lanes.toml`
3. `@docs/testing/console.md` in CLAUDE.md §11
4. `console:` in the justfile, running vitest
5. a `console:` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` whose steps run
   `just console`

All five land in one commit, which is what `scripts/check-lane-manifest.sh`
enforces in both directions.

The lane covers the pure derivations (chart scales, byte and count formatting,
the search-parameter codecs, the Schema decoders against recorded response
bodies) and the presentational components under Testing Library with injected
props. The build verb is separate and named `web`, the way `just wasm` is the
build and `just workerd` is the lane.

### Files phase 3 touches

`web/` (new: `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`,
`index.html`, `src/`, `test/`), `crates/cachet-worker/src/api.rs` and
`crates/cachet-api/src/lib.rs` for the `fontCss` field, `infra/src/config.ts`
and `infra/alchemy.run.ts` for the variable, `justfile`,
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/testing/lanes.toml`,
`docs/testing/console.md` (new), `CLAUDE.md` §11.

---

## Phase 4: the documents catch up

Four ADRs and five documents, following `docs/adr/README.md`'s format. The
next free number is 0014.

- **ADR 0014, the console is served by the deployment.** Why the same worker
  and the same origin (the session cookie is SameSite=Lax and no CORS layer
  exists), why `run_worker_first` is true rather than a glob list (a protocol
  path added later must not be able to start serving the app shell), and why
  `/console` rather than the root.
- **ADR 0015, the counters answer time and filtered questions.** Why the
  bucket joins the dimension enum, why `(bucket, window)` pairs are validated,
  why filters are limited to closed enums, and why the SQL API's base URL
  became a variable.
- **ADR 0016, the browser session is see-only.** A refinement of ADR 0002,
  recording that a session authenticates the console's surface and is refused
  on cache object reads, and that the 14-day statistics window is an accepted
  trade rather than an oversight.
- **`docs/console.md`**, the console's own document: what each screen answers,
  which route each panel reads, and the states listed in 3d. One
  `@docs/console.md` line in CLAUDE.md §11, unfenced and unbackticked, or
  `scripts/check-doc-manifest.sh` fails on the fourth assertion.
- **`docs/DEPLOY.md`**: a console section, the `CACHET_DEPLOY_FONT_CSS` row,
  the corrected `CACHET_DEPLOY_UI_ORIGIN` row, the `double2`-for-writes
  definition, the new query parameters on `/api/self/events`, and a
  `CACHET_DEPLOY_STATS_TOKEN` row saying that reporting needs
  `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` in the deploy environment as well, because the
  worker now carries it.
- **`docs/security/threat-model.md`**: the corrected session sentence, the
  console's origin, and the third-party font CDN.
- **`README.md`**: an admin section beside the laptop and CI ones.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: §1's "the future SPA" becomes the console, and §4 names
  `web/` alongside the crates.

---

## Verification

Run the local gates in the order the phases land. `just check` is the
pre-push parity verb, though note it does not currently run `workerd`, so run
that one by hand.

```
nix develop
just unit property golden
just openapi && just openapi-check
just wasm && just workerd
just web && just console
just check
```

Then prove the console end to end against a real deployment. Staging deploys
automatically after a green `ci` on main, so the fastest path is a merge; to
rehearse locally instead:

```
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=... CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=... just deploy cachet-staging
CACHET_INTEGRATION_URL=https://<staging host> just integration
```

Before the browser checks, confirm the binding fix on the deployment itself,
because this is the first time the route can answer at all:

```
curl -sS --netrc-file ~/.netrc \
  "https://<staging host>/api/self/events?subject=reads&by=day&window=week"
```

It answers 200 with seven rows in ascending date order, zeros included. A 503
`storage_unavailable` means the account id still is not reaching the worker.

By hand in a browser, against staging, confirm each of these:

1. `https://<host>/` redirects to `/console`, and an unauthenticated visit
   shows the sign-in screen rather than a 401 body.
2. Sign-in through GitHub lands back on `/console` with the session cookie
   set, and the status bar names your login.
3. All five screens render with live numbers, and Traffic's Day, Week, and
   Month controls each change the line's bucket count to 24, 7, and 30.
4. Laptops shows a non-zero share, which proves the cross-filter reached the
   query.
5. `curl -s https://<host>/<some absent hash>.narinfo` still answers 404
   `application/problem+json`, and `nix copy --from https://<host>` still
   substitutes a pushed path. This is the assertion the whole serving design
   exists to protect, and the integration lane's step 5 already covers the
   second half.
6. A second GitHub account that is an org member but absent from
   `CACHET_ADMINS` sees Access and nothing else.
7. Copy your `cachet_session` cookie out of the browser and replay it against
   a narinfo path. It answers 401, and the same cookie still answers
   `/api/self/stats`.

The integration lane gains one step for the first and fifth of those, so the
round trip is proven by `just integration` rather than by memory.

## Addendum: the HUD strip is live

The `hud-strip` frame carries four values on every screen, and no route
serves any of them today.

`CACHET · PRODUCTION · V1.2.0 · A4F31C` is the deployment's identity. The
worker knows its host and not its name, so `infra/alchemy.run.ts` binds
`CACHET_DEPLOY_NAME` from the stage it already computes, and
`/api/public/config` grows `deployment`, `version`, and `buildSha`. Version
comes from `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`. The build sha comes from
`option_env!("CACHET_BUILD_SHA")`, which the `wasm` recipe sets from
`git rev-parse --short=6 HEAD` before calling worker-build, so a plain
`cargo build` leaves it absent rather than lying.

`UTC 05:14:02` needs no route. Every response already carries a `Date`
header, so the console takes its offset from the last answer and ticks
locally. That shows the deployment's clock rather than the laptop's, which
is what a HUD beside a deployment name means.

`NEXT COLLECTION IN 23 H 46 M` and `● HEALTHY` come from a new admin route,
`GET /api/self/health`, answering `status`, `nextCollectionAtMs`,
`latestRunId`, `latestFinishedAtMs`, and `gate`. The cron expression lives in
the alchemy program alone, so it binds as `CACHET_GC_CRON` and a total parser
in `cachet-core` recognizes the daily `M H * * *` shape and answers the next
UTC instant, or answers nothing for any other shape so the console hides the
countdown rather than inventing one. Status is derived: `healthy` when the
latest report exists, tripped no gate, and finished within two cron periods;
`degraded` when it tripped a gate or is older than that; `unknown` on a
deployment with no report yet.

The split matters for a non-admin. Identity and the clock ride
`/api/public/config` and the `Date` header, which an org member can read, so
their HUD renders with the countdown and the status dot omitted rather than
the strip failing.
PLANEOF

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSGEOF'
The counters answer time and filtered questions, and the account they query under reaches the worker

/api/self/events could never answer. api.rs reads
env.var("CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID") on every request and the alchemy program
never bound it, so every deployment answered 503 storage_unavailable,
including one configured with a stats token. The counting worked; the
reporting had not run once since the route shipped. loadStageConfig now
refuses a stats token that arrives without an account id, because half a
credential is a chart that never loads rather than an error anyone sees.

The route grows the two questions the console's charts need. by=hour and
by=day group into time buckets and answer a series: oldest first, one row
per bucket, zeros included, each dimension the bucket's first instant in
epoch seconds. A bucket finer than its window can hold is refused rather
than truncated, because a truncated series is a chart that silently
starts partway through its own window. kind, outcome, and actor narrow an
answer to one value each, which is what makes "laptop reads by outcome"
askable.

Filters mean the writer's vocabulary had to close. StatKind and
StatOutcome replace the free strings, so a filter value parses into the
same set the writers emit before anything is formatted into SQL, and one
test now ties the two sides together where a comment used to name the
risk. Analytics Engine reports nothing for a bucket nothing happened in,
so the fill is what stops a chart drawing a straight line through an
empty hour; the property lane holds it whole, and found the epoch
boundary where the window ran off the front and the series ended in the
future.

Three things the vocabularies exposed. Writes never measured their bytes,
so "pushed this week" had no source; they now count content-length, which
is what the bucket grew by. The multipart open and completion branches
returned past the counter, so begin and complete were kinds the router
named and no point ever carried. And by=project could only ever answer
one empty row, because nothing had ever filled blob6; the dimension is
gone and the column stays reserved, since renumbering would misread every
point already written.

GET /api/whoami answers who a request authenticates as, admin or not: a
console that could only learn its standing by provoking a 403 would make
a refusal part of loading a page. A browser session stops being a
cache-read credential in the same change, because it could substitute
from the cache with a cookie that outlives org membership by a fortnight,
and nix never sends a cookie.

The two bodies the worker streams verbatim, a GC report and a lease, are
mirrored in cachet-api so the document describes them, with a test that
decodes the core types' own bytes to keep the mirrors honest.

# ADR 0015: The counter route answers time and filtered questions

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-08-26
- **Context doc:** [../../CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) §1;
  [../security/threat-model.md](../security/threat-model.md)

## Context

`GET /api/self/events` shipped answering one question shape: totals for
one subject grouped by one blob column over one window, largest first.
The console's screens need two shapes it could not produce. A line of
reads per day is a group by time, and time is not a blob column. Laptop
reads split by outcome is a filter, and the route took none, so the only
way to ask about one caller class was to group by that class and lose
every other dimension.

Both are easy to add carelessly. The credential behind the route is a
Cloudflare API token, and the route's whole safety argument is that no
caller text reaches the statement: a value is either a literal in the
source or something an enum produced. A `WHERE blob4 = '<caller text>'`
would end that argument, and a `GROUP BY <caller text>` would end it
faster.

There was also a reason nobody had noticed the route did not work. The
worker read `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and the alchemy program never bound
it, so every deployment answered 503; and the workerd lane bound no
analytics token, so every lane row was refused at the configuration
check before any query ran. The success path had no coverage at all.

## Decision

1. Time buckets join the dimension enum as `hour` and `day`, so `by=day`
   is the same parameter as `by=actor`. A time dimension emits a
   projection rather than a column name, orders ascending rather than by
   count, and bounds itself by the bucket count its window implies.
2. The pair is validated. A bucket finer than its window can hold
   (hourly over a month is 720 rows against a cap of 100) is refused with
   400 `malformed_query`. Truncating instead would answer a chart that
   silently begins partway through its own window.
3. A bucketed answer is gap-filled by the worker before it is served.
   Analytics Engine returns no row for a bucket nothing happened in, so
   the raw answer has holes and a line drawn through them claims traffic
   was smooth when it was absent. The fill is pure, lives in cachet-core,
   and is held by a property-lane law.
4. Filters narrow on `kind`, `outcome`, and `actor` only. Those three
   columns hold values from vocabularies the writers define, so a filter
   value parses into an enum before anything is formatted. `repository`
   and `reference` hold text a pusher chose; they stay groupable and
   never filterable, because a `GROUP BY` names a column where a filter
   names a value.
5. The writers' vocabularies became enums (`StatKind`, `StatOutcome`) to
   make point 4 possible, which also ties the blob order to the query
   mapping with a test where a comment used to name the risk.
6. The SQL API's base address is a variable, `CACHET_STATS_API_URL`,
   defaulting to Cloudflare's. The lane points it at a stub that receives
   the composed statement as text and answers rows the scenario chose.
7. The deployment binds `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, and a deploy that sets
   a stats token without one is refused by name rather than deployed into
   a 503.

## Consequences

The console's charts have queries behind them, and the questions they ask
are the questions the route offers rather than questions it composes. The
statement is now asserted byte-for-byte in the lane instead of by four
substring checks, which is the right strength for a statement that runs
with an account token.

The route's success path is covered for the first time: the answer, the
row deserialization, the shaping, the fill, and the exact SQL for each
combination. `storage_unavailable` also gained a deterministic wire
assertion, because the stub can refuse on demand.

The cost is a second address the worker can be pointed at. It is
transport configuration rather than authority, the way `CACHET_JWKS_URL`
already is: the token is what authorises the query, and an operator who
can set worker variables can already set the token.

## Alternatives considered

**A separate `bucket=` parameter beside `by=`.** It would allow a
two-dimensional answer, reads per day split by outcome. Rejected for now:
nothing asks for it, and it doubles the shapes the response type has to
describe. Adding it later is compatible with this.

**Formatted dates as the bucket's name.** Rejected: the answer would then
depend on the SQL engine's calendar formatting, and every reader would
have to agree with it. Epoch seconds mean one thing.

**Filtering on `repository` with an escaped value.** Rejected: escaping
is a weaker claim than absence, and the threat model's sentence about
caller text never reaching the statement is worth more than the
convenience. A repository drill-down can group by the column instead.

**Fixing the account-id binding alone and leaving the lane blind.**
Rejected: the binding bug survived a release precisely because no test
could reach the code it broke, so the seam and the stub are the fix.
MDEOF
cat > docs/adr/0016-the-browser-session-is-see-only.md <<'MDEOF'
# ADR 0016: The browser session is see-only

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-08-26
- **Context doc:** [0002-three-authentication-flows.md](0002-three-authentication-flows.md);
  [../security/threat-model.md](../security/threat-model.md)

## Context

ADR 0002 gave browsers the third credential: an OAuth code flow against
the worker, a KV session record, and an HttpOnly cookie. The session was
resolved by the same `authorize_read` every other read credential goes
through, and nothing downstream distinguished it, so a session cookie
authenticated narinfo and NAR reads exactly as a laptop's token did.

Two facts about that cookie make it a worse credential than the ones
beside it. It is sent automatically by the browser to every path on the
origin, which is what cookies do. And its record holds a login and a
creation time and no GitHub credential, so unlike a laptop's issued token
there is nothing to re-check membership with: the session is accepted
until its fourteen-day expiry. A person who left the org kept a working
cache-read credential for up to a fortnight, and the threat model claimed
otherwise, describing a 600-second verdict re-check the code did not
perform.

Building the console made this matter more, because the console is the
reason sessions exist at all and it made them common.

## Decision

1. A session identity authenticates the console's own surface:
   `/api/self/*`, `/api/whoami`, `/api/probe`, and `/roots`.
2. It is refused on the paths that serve cache bytes, `{hash}.narinfo`
   and `/nar/{key}`, with 401 `unauthorized`: the same answer an
   anonymous read gets, because naming the reason would tell a caller
   which credential class it holds.
3. The fourteen-day window on the console's surface stands, and the
   threat model says so plainly instead of claiming a re-check.

## Consequences

Nothing that reads for real loses a credential: nix reads through a
netrc, and the daemon never sends a cookie. What the change removes is a
credential that could be copied out of a browser's cookie jar and used to
substitute from the cache.

An ex-member's session can still read counters and collection reports
until it expires or an operator deletes it. That is a narrower thing to
be exposed than the cache's contents, and it is now the written bound
rather than an unwritten one.

The console gains nothing to work around: every screen it has reads the
surface a session still authenticates.

## Alternatives considered

**Store the GitHub token on the session record and re-check membership,
the way ADR 0002 does for laptops.** This would close the counter window
to 600 seconds as well. Rejected for now: it puts a second GitHub
credential at rest in KV (ADR 0003 weighs that cost) to shorten exposure
of a surface that shows counts rather than contents. If the console ever
serves something worth a tighter bound, this is the change to make.

**Shorten `SESSION_TTL_MS`.** Rejected: it trades the window against how
often a person has to sign in again, and it would not have stopped a
copied cookie from substituting within the window.

**Correct the threat model to match the code and change nothing.**
Rejected: it leaves the console's own credential as the only one that can
read the cache without its holder's org membership ever being rechecked.
MDEOF

input.command:
cat > docs/adr/0014-the-deployment-serves-its-own-console.md <<'MDEOF'
# ADR 0014: The deployment serves its own console

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-08-26
- **Context doc:** [../../CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) §1;
  [0002-three-authentication-flows.md](0002-three-authentication-flows.md)

## Context

The console is a browser application that reads a deployment's counters,
collection reports, and access configuration. Where it is served from
decides three other things at once.

The credential settles the first. ADR 0002 gave browsers a session
cookie, and that cookie is `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`.
SameSite=Lax means a cross-site request never carries it, and the worker
emits no `Access-Control-*` headers and answers `OPTIONS` with a 404. A
console on another origin would need a CORS layer, a second credential,
or both. Served from the worker's own host it needs none of that, and
`require_admin` already accepts a session identity, so every admin route
works the day the files land.

The second is the nix key space, and it is the one that can break the
deployment's real job. A binary cache is read by asking about paths, and
most of those paths are not in any given cache: nix reads a 404 as "ask
the next substituter" and moves on. Cloudflare's asset layer has a
`not_found_handling` mode that answers an unmatched request with an
application shell, which is the right behavior for an application and a
catastrophe here, because it turns every cache miss into `200 text/html`
and every substituter into a client parsing HTML as a narinfo.

The third is what the deployment costs to run. Serving the console from
its own worker, or from Pages, means a second deployable, a second
domain, and a second thing to keep in step with the first.

## Decision

1. The worker's own deployment carries the console as static assets,
   mounted under `/console`. `GET /` answers 302 to `/console`, because
   nix asks for `/nix-cache-info` and for paths and never for the root.
2. Both of the asset layer's handling modes are off. `notFoundHandling`
   is `none`, so a request matching no file falls through to the worker
   and is routed as it always was. `htmlHandling` is `none`, so the layer
   performs no trailing-slash redirects and `/console` reaches the
   router.
3. The router owns the console's own routes. A path under `/console`
   whose last segment has no extension is a route inside the console's
   router, and the worker serves the shell for it through the `ASSETS`
   binding. Deciding by extension rather than by a list of screens means
   adding a screen changes the console alone.
4. A worker deployed without the binding answers 404 for `/console` and
   serves the protocol exactly as before, which is the same degradation
   the counter binding already makes.
5. The OAuth callback lands on `https://{host}/console` by default.
   `CACHET_UI_ORIGIN` stays as an override for a UI hosted elsewhere, and
   set to the empty string it means the deployment has no UI and the
   callback answers 204.

## Consequences

The console is one more directory in the same deploy: `just deploy`
builds it, alchemy uploads it beside the wasm bundle, and there is no
second domain, no CORS layer, and no second credential. Signing in works
with no configuration at all.

Asset requests are answered by Cloudflare without invoking the worker, so
the console costs nothing per file served. The worker is invoked only for
the console's own routes, which is one request per page load.

The workerd lane cannot bind assets and test the collector in the same
process: under miniflare, binding assets puts Cloudflare's asset router
in front of the worker, and that router has no scheduled handler, so the
collector's dev endpoint answers "exception". The console scenario boots
against a generated copy of the lane config with the asset block appended
and every other scenario runs without it. Production invokes the cron
against the worker itself, so this is a limitation of the local runner.

## Alternatives considered

**`run_worker_first: true`, with the Rust router deciding every path.**
This was the first decision, and it was wrong for a reason worth
recording: it puts the worker in front of `/cdn-cgi/*`, which the
platform and the local runner reserve for themselves. It broke the
collector's dev endpoint immediately, and the set of platform paths it
would break in production is not something this repository can
enumerate. Turning both handling modes off achieves the same protection
by never letting the layer decide anything.

**`notFoundHandling: "single-page-application"` with a `runWorkerFirst`
glob list naming the protocol paths.** Rejected: a protocol path added
later without updating the glob list would silently begin serving the
console's shell to nix clients, which is precisely the drift class
CLAUDE.md §0 exists to prevent.

**A separate console worker on `console.<host>`, binding this one.**
Rejected: it needs the CORS layer and the cross-site cookie problem that
serving from one origin avoids, and it doubles the deployment for an
admin surface with a handful of readers.

**Serving the console from the root rather than `/console`.** Rejected as
close to free but not free: the root is unclaimed today, and a console
there would mean the deployment's protocol surface and its application
surface share a namespace forever. A prefix keeps the two apart and
costs one redirect.
MDEOF
python3 - <<'PY'
p='docs/DEPLOY.md'
s=open(p).read()
old = '''| `CACHET_DEPLOY_UI_ORIGIN` | no | Browser login's redirect target; unset answers 204 instead. |'''
new = '''| `CACHET_DEPLOY_UI_ORIGIN` | no | Where browser login lands. Unset lands on this deployment's own console; set it to override, or to the empty string for a deployment with no UI. |'''
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)

old = '''## Verifying a deployment'''
new = '''## The console

Every deployment serves a browser console at `https://<host>/console`,
and its root redirects there. Sign in with GitHub through the same OAuth
App the CLI uses; an admin sees the collection reports, the counters, and
the access configuration, and an org member outside `CACHET_ADMINS` sees
the access screen alone.

It ships as static files uploaded beside the worker, so `just deploy`
builds it and nothing else needs configuring. The asset layer answers a
request that names one of those files and never invents an answer for one
that does not: a request matching no file falls through to the worker,
which routes it the way it always has. That is what keeps a cache miss a

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSGEOF'
The deployment serves its own console, and a cache miss stays a cache miss

The console mounts as static assets under /console on the worker's own
deployment, and the root redirects there. Same origin is what makes the
session cookie work at all: it is SameSite=Lax on Path=/, the worker
emits no Access-Control headers and 404s OPTIONS, and require_admin
already accepts a session, so every admin route works the day the files
land. Signing in needs no configuration either, because the callback now
defaults to this deployment's own console; CACHET_UI_ORIGIN stays as an
override, and set empty it still means "no UI".

Both of the asset layer's handling modes are off, and that is the whole
safety argument. A binary cache is read by asking about paths that mostly
are not in it, and nix reads a 404 as "ask the next substituter". An
asset layer answering an unmatched request with an application shell
turns every cache miss into 200 text/html and every substituter into a
client parsing HTML as a narinfo. With notFoundHandling none, a request
matching no file falls through to the router and is decided the way it
always was; the router serves the shell only for paths under /console
whose last segment has no extension, so adding a screen changes the
console alone.

run_worker_first was the first answer and it was wrong. It puts the
worker in front of /cdn-cgi/*, which the platform and the local runner
reserve: it broke the collector's dev endpoint immediately, and the set
of platform paths it would break in production is not something this
repository can enumerate. ADR 0014 records that, along with why the
console is a prefix rather than the root.

The lane pays one cost for this. Binding assets under miniflare puts
Cloudflare's asset router in front of the worker, and that router has no
scheduled handler, so the collector's dev endpoint answers "exception"
with assets bound. The console scenario boots against a generated copy of
the lane config with the asset block appended, rather than a second
committed config that would drift from the first, and every other
scenario runs without it. Its rows include the one this design exists
for: an absent narinfo and an absent NAR still answer 404 text/plain with
the negative caching headers and never the shell.
MSGEOF
